requirements.text: Proposals must address issues in one or more of the specified areas: rural technician education, broadening participation (including veterans), recruiting/retaining students with disabilities, or emerging industry needs.
requirements.source_quote: The ATE program is interested in projects addressing issues in: 1) rural technician education; 2) projects that broaden the participation of the full spectrum of diverse talent that society has to offer in the entry-level technical workforce including strategies to recruit veterans into technician education programs; 3) projects that focus on recruiting, retaining and completing students with disabilities into STEM technician education programs; and 4) projects that support emerging industry needs for skilled technical workers, for example, industry needs for technicians with AI knowledge and skills.

requirements.text: Projects must have an institutional impact.

requirements.source_quote: The curricular focus and the activities of all projects should demonstrably contribute to the ATE program's central goals: producing more qualified science and engineering technicians to meet workforce demands, and improving the technical skills and the general science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) preparation of these technicians and the educators who prepare them.

requirements.text: Courses developed or updated must be credit-bearing courses with the potential to contribute to or result in an academic credential.

requirements.source_quote: Institutions may also make use of their non-credit bearing offerings if they can demonstrate increased opportunities to engage incumbent workers and convert these offerings to academic credit.

requirements.text: Proposals must demonstrate a thorough awareness of previous relevant ATE grants, research on effective technician education, and contemporary developments in the relevant field(s) of technology.

requirements.text: Proposers are encouraged to contact PIs of previously funded projects and centers to explore possibilities for adapting materials, evaluating materials, receiving guidance, or collaborating.

requirements.text: The evaluation plan must describe formative and summative evaluation roles.
requirements.source_quote: The primary role of the evaluator is to analyze collected data to summarize findings and inform project team decision making about any modifications to the implementation of the project activities (i.e., formative evaluation). At the end of the project, the project evaluator should provide a summative evaluation identifying key accomplishments, their impacts, and lessons learned.

requirements.text: The evaluation plan must show clear alignment with project goals, objectives, outcomes, activities, and deliverables.

requirements.text: Surveys must be developed in partnership between project team members and the evaluator.

requirements.text: Specific data sources, instruments, and methods must be identified in the evaluation plan.

requirements.text: A timeline for evaluative activities including data collection, report submission, and communication frequency must be included.

requirements.text: Discussion with a program officer is strongly encouraged prior to submitting an unsolicited proposal.
requirements.source_quote: Discussion with a program officer is strongly encouraged prior to submitting an unsolicited proposal to the ATE program.

requirements.text: Funds for equipment and instrumentation normally may not exceed $300,000 for the duration of a full project grant, with exceptions for single pieces costing more than $300,000 if justified for student use/learning outcomes.
requirements.source_quote: Funds requested for equipment and instrumentation essential to meet the goals and objectives of the project normally may not exceed $300,000 for the duration of a full project grant. Exceptions to this limit will be considered when a single piece of equipment costs more than $300,000, and the need for the equipment is justified in terms of student use and learning outcomes.

requirements.text: Equipment requests to update an existing program may exceed the $300,000 limit if the need is validated by industry.
requirements.source_quote: If instrumentation is requested to update an existing program, the request may exceed the $300,000 limitation if the need for the equipment is validated by industry.

requirements.text: Equipment requests for Track 1: Small Scale Projects must be within the overall scope of the project budget.
requirements.source_quote: Equipment requests for Track 1: Small Scale Projects must be within the overall scope of the project budget.

requirements.text: Proposers must request educational discounts from equipment suppliers and explain any discount in the budget justification.
requirements.source_quote: It is expected that the proposer will request educational discounts from the equipment supplier, and that any discount will be explained in the budget justification.

requirements.text: Equipment requests must be clearly disclosed in the proposal budget and justified in the budget justification.
requirements.source_quote: Equipment requests must be clearly disclosed in the proposal budget and justified in the budget justification.

requirements.text: NSF funds may not be used for expenditures that would normally be made in the absence of an award, such as routine teaching activities and laboratory upgrades.
requirements.source_quote: NSF funds may not be used to support expenditures that would normally be made in the absence of an award, such as costs for routine teaching activities and laboratory upgrades (supplies and computers).

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for equipment and supplies for common laboratory or instructional needs (e.g., computer labs, smart classrooms, general laptops, projectors, cameras, etc.).
requirements.source_quote: Equipment and related materials and supplies that an institution would normally purchase to serve common laboratory or instructional needs (e.g. computer labs, "smart" classrooms, general purpose laptop computers, projectors, cameras, audio devices, videoconferencing software, webcasting software);

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for common productivity software and teaching aids.
requirements.source_quote: Common productivity software (e.g. Microsoft Office, Microsoft Project, Adobe Creative Cloud) and teaching aids (e.g. "drill and practice" software);

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for replacement equipment or instrumentation that does not significantly improve instructional capability.
requirements.source_quote: Replacement equipment or instrumentation that does not significantly improve instructional capability;

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for vehicles, trailers, laboratory furnishings, general utility items (office equipment, benches, tables, desks, chairs, storage cases), and routine supplies.
requirements.source_quote: Vehicles, trailers, laboratory furnishings, or general utility items such as office equipment, benches, tables, desks, chairs, storage cases, and routine supplies;

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for maintenance equipment and maintenance or service contracts unless the contract is built into the initial cost of the equipment.
requirements.source_quote: Maintenance equipment and maintenance or service contracts, unless the maintenance or service contract is built into the initial cost of the equipment;

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for construction, renovation, or modernization of rooms, laboratories, or other facilities.
requirements.source_quote: Construction, renovation, or modernization of rooms, laboratories or other facilities;

requirements.text: NSF project funds may not be used for the installation of equipment or instrumentation (distinct from on-site assembly of multi-component instruments).
requirements.source_quote: The installation of equipment or instrumentation (as distinct from the on-site assembly of multi-component instruments--which is an allowable charge).

requirements.text: Salaries of administrative and clerical staff should normally be treated as indirect costs; direct charging is only appropriate if specific conditions in PAPPG and 2 CFR § 200.413 are met.
requirements.source_quote: In accordance with NSF Administrative and Clerical Salaries and Wages Policy (see PAPPG Chapter II.D.2.f(i)(b) and 2 CFR § 200.413), the salaries of administrative and clerical staff should normally be treated as indirect costs (F&A). Direct charging of these costs may be appropriate only if all the conditions specified in the PAPPG and in section 413(c) of the Uniform Guidance are met.

requirements.text: Reasonable travel costs, subsistence (lodging and meals), and specific justified stipends per meeting day for participants may be included in project budgets for professional development conferences.
requirements.source_quote: In proposals that involve professional development activities, reasonable associated travel costs and costs for subsistence (lodging and meals) may be included in project budgets. In addition, funds may be requested for a reasonable stipend per meeting day for participants; requests for such stipends must be specific to the target audience and must be fully justified

requirements.text: NSF funds can be used to hire substitute teachers if necessary to meet project goals, if they directly replace participating teachers, paid per district policy, and records are maintained.
requirements.source_quote: The use of NSF funds to hire substitute teachers is allowed under the following conditions: (1) it is necessary to meet the goals and objectives of the project; and (2) it can be documented that the substitute teachers are directly replacing teachers participating in the NSF-funded project. Substitute teachers should be paid in accordance with established school district policies, and in lieu of paying the teachers participating in the project. Records must be maintained on the hiring and use of substitutes.

requirements.text: Extra service pay (overload compensation) must follow 2 CFR § 200.430, be subject to uniform institutional policies, and if paid as a stipend, converted to reflect additional total salary compensation under Personnel budget category.
requirements.source_quote: Please follow 2 CFR § 200.430. Extra service pay normally represents overload compensation, subject to institutional compensation policies above and beyond the Institutional Base Salary (IBS). The institution must have written policies that apply uniformly to all faculty, not just those working on a federal award. For institutions that support extra service pay through payment of a stipend this amount must be converted to reflect the additional total salary compensation under the budget category for Personnel

requirements.text: The proposal should include only the names of NVC members who have agreed to serve.
requirements.source_quote: The proposal should include only the names of NVC members who have agreed to serve should an award be made.

requirements.text: The proposal should address how the NVC will be used in the project.
requirements.source_quote: The proposal should address how the NVC will be used in the project.

requirements.text: Funds to support an independent evaluator must be requested, matching the scope of proposed evaluative activities developed in partnership with the project team.
requirements.source_quote: The funds to support an evaluator independent of the project must be requested. The requested funds must match the scope of the proposed evaluative activities that have been developed in partnership with the Center/project team.

requirements.text: An evaluator employed by the home institution is allowed only if they work in a separate organizational unit with a different reporting line.
requirements.source_quote: The evaluator may be employed by a project's home institution, as long as he or she works in a separate organizational unit (e.g., a different department) that has a different reporting line than that of the project's home unit.

requirements.text: The project should define how data will be collected by the project team or evaluator for analysis by the evaluator.
requirements.source_quote: define how data will be collected by the project team or evaluator for analysis by the evaluator.

requirements.text: The full proposal deadline is October 03, 2024.
requirements.source_quote: October 03, 2024

requirements.text: Thereafter, the full proposal deadline is the first Thursday in October annually.
requirements.source_quote: First Thursday in October, Annually Thereafter

requirements.text: Organizations must register with Grants.gov to create an institutional profile before using it for the first time.
requirements.source_quote: Before using Grants.gov for the first time, each organization must register to create an institutional profile.

requirements.text: The Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) must submit the application to Grants.gov and verify the desired funding opportunity and agency.
requirements.source_quote: the Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) must submit the application to Grants.gov and verify the desired funding opportunity and agency to which the application is submitted.

requirements.text: The AOR must sign and submit the application to Grants.gov.
requirements.source_quote: The AOR must then sign and submit the application to Grants.gov.

requirements.text: Proposers who submitted via Research.gov may use Research.gov to verify the status of their submission.
requirements.source_quote: Proposers that submitted via Research.gov may use Research.gov to verify the status of their submission to NSF.

requirements.text: For proposers submitting via Grants.gov, the AOR may check application status on Grants.gov only until the application has been received and validated by NSF.
requirements.source_quote: For proposers that submitted via Grants.gov, until an application has been received and validated by NSF, the Authorized Organizational Representative may check the status of an application on Grants.gov.

requirements.text: After receiving email notification from NSF, proposers must use Research.gov to check the status of their application.
requirements.source_quote: After proposers have received an e-mail notification from NSF, Research.gov should be used to check the status of an application.

requirements.text: Proposers are invited to suggest names of persons they believe are especially well qualified to review the proposal and/or persons they would prefer not review the proposal.
requirements.source_quote: Proposers are invited to suggest names of persons they believe are especially well qualified to review the proposal and/or persons they would prefer not review the proposal.
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: Submission of suggested reviewers is optional.
requirements.source_quote: Submission of such names, however, is optional.
requirements.source_heading: VI. NSF Proposal Processing And Review Procedures

requirements.text: Proposals should be of the highest quality with the potential to advance or transform frontiers of knowledge.
requirements.source_quote: All NSF projects should be of the highest quality and have the potential to advance, if not transform, the frontiers of knowledge.
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Projects must contribute more broadly to achieving societal goals through research, directly related activities, or complementary supported activities, with all methods well justified.
requirements.source_quote: NSF projects, in the aggregate, should contribute more broadly to achieving societal goals. These "Broader Impacts" may be accomplished through the research itself, through activities that are directly related to specific research projects, or through activities that are supported by, but are complementary to, the project. The project activities may be based on previously established and/or innovative methods and approaches, but in either case must be well justified.
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Individual projects must include clearly stated goals, specific descriptions of intended activities, and a plan to document outputs.
requirements.source_quote: Thus, individual projects should include clearly stated goals, specific descriptions of the activities that the PI intends to do, and a plan in place to document the outputs of those activities.
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: The Project Description must address what proposers want to do, why, how, how success will be measured, and potential benefits.
requirements.source_quote: When evaluating NSF proposals, reviewers will be asked to consider what the proposers want to do, why they want to do it, how they plan to do it, how they will know if they succeed, and what benefits could accrue if the project is successful.
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Proposals must explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts.
requirements.source_quote: 2. To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original, or potentially transformative concepts?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: The plan for carrying out activities must be well-reasoned, well-organized, based on sound rationale, and incorporate a mechanism to assess success.
requirements.source_quote: 3. Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized, and based on a sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Proposals must demonstrate that the individual, team, or organization is well qualified to conduct the proposed activities.
requirements.source_quote: 4. How well qualified is the individual, team, or organization to conduct the proposed activities?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Proposals must demonstrate that adequate resources are available to carry out the proposed activities.
requirements.source_quote: 5. Are there adequate resources available to the PI (either at the home organization or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Proposers must prepare a Data Management and Sharing Plan, which reviewers will evaluate as appropriate.
requirements.source_quote: Proposers are reminded that reviewers will also be asked to review the Data Management and Sharing Plan and the Mentoring Plan, as appropriate.
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: The project must have potential for improving student learning in science or engineering technician education programs with detailed goals, objectives and activities.
requirements.source_quote: Does the project have potential for improving student learning in science or engineering technician education programs with detailed goals, objectives and activities?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: The rationale for selecting activities must be clearly articulated, informed by research literature, and build on that base and the work of others.
requirements.source_quote: Is the rationale for selecting particular activities or components for development or adaptation clearly articulated and informed by the research literature? Does the work build on that base and the work of others?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: The evaluation plan must be tied to project outcomes, provide for effective assessment of student learning, and likely provide useful information.
requirements.source_quote: Is the evaluation plan clearly tied to the project outcomes, provide for effective assessment of student learning, and likely to provide useful information to the project and others?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Evidence of institutional and industry support must be clear and compelling, and plans for long-term institutionalization must be addressed.
requirements.source_quote: Is the evidence of institutional and industry support clear and compelling, and have plans for long-term institutionalization been addressed?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: An assessment of workforce needs for technicians must be conducted, and the project should work with employers to address their current and future needs.
requirements.source_quote: Has an assessment of workforce needs for technicians been conducted? Does the project work with employers to address their current and future needs for technicians?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Project results must be widely disseminated, products distributed effectively, and commercialized when appropriate.
requirements.source_quote: Will the project's results be widely disseminated and will its products be distributed effectively and commercialized when appropriate?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Results and products must be adaptable at other institutions.
requirements.source_quote: Are the results and products of the project adaptable at other institutions?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: The project must promote the participation of the full spectrum of diverse talent in the technical workforce.
requirements.source_quote: Does the project promote the participation of the full spectrum of diverse talent that society has to offer in the technical workforce?
requirements.source_heading: A. Merit Review Principles and Criteria

requirements.text: Funding for infrastructure projects must use iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials produced in the United States.
requirements.source_quote: no funding made available through this funding opportunity may be obligated for infrastructure projects under an award unless all iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials used in the project are produced in the United States.

requirements.text: Executive branch policy requires maximizing the use of goods, products, and materials produced in, and services offered in, the United States.
requirements.source_quote: it is the policy of the executive branch to use terms and conditions of Federal financial assistance awards to maximize, consistent with law, the use of goods, products, and materials produced in, and services offered in, the United States.

requirements.text: Submit an annual project report to the Program Officer no later than 90 days before the end of the budget period (unless a program requires more frequent reporting).
requirements.source_quote: the Principal Investigator must submit an annual project report to the cognizant Program Officer no later than 90 days prior to the end of the current budget period.

requirements.text: Submit a final annual project report no later than 120 days after the grant expires.
requirements.source_quote: No later than 120 days following expiration of a grant, the PI also is required to submit a final annual project report

requirements.text: Submit a project outcomes report for the general public no later than 120 days after the grant expires.
requirements.source_quote: and a project outcomes report for the general public.

requirements.text: Use NSF's electronic system (Research.gov) to prepare and submit annual and final annual reports.
requirements.source_quote: PIs are required to use NSF's electronic project-reporting system, available through Research.gov, for preparation and submission of annual and final annual project reports.

requirements.text: Use NSF's electronic system (Research.gov) to prepare and submit the project outcomes report.
requirements.source_quote: The project outcomes report also must be prepared and submitted using Research.gov.

requirements.text: Respond annually to the ATE Annual Survey conducted by the EvaluATE Resource Hub, providing specific data on students, educators, retention, placement, impact, and quality indicators.
requirements.source_quote: All PIs are required to respond annually to this survey that requests information about the number and characteristics of students and educators that have been affected by the project; the retention, graduation, and placement rates for students; the project's impact on workforce needs; awards and other measures of the quality of the project's products and activities; and other indicators of the project's effect on the quality and quantity of technicians being educated for the high-tech workplace.

requirements.text: Work with ATE Central to archive digital deliverables (e.g., curriculum, materials) by providing copies in an archivable format with clear intellectual property information.
requirements.source_quote: Specifically, projects and centers that create resources that exist in digital form (e.g., curriculum, professional development, and recruitment materials) must provide copies of those resources in appropriate format and with clear intellectual property information to ATE Central for archiving purposes, in an archivable format and with clear intellectual property information.

requirements.text: License new materials created with grant support under a Creative Commons Attribution license (CC BY, CC BY-SA, or CC BY-NC-SA), except for software source code.
requirements.source_quote: Additionally, it is suggested that the developer of new materials license all work (except for computer software source code, discussed below) created with the support of the grant under either the 3.0 Unsupported or 3.0 United States version of the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY), Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA), or Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike (CC BY-NC-SA) license.

requirements.text: Release computer software source code developed with ATE grant funds under an open license acceptable to the Free Software Foundation and/or the Open Source Initiative.
requirements.source_quote: Recipients may release all new source code developed or created with ATE grant funds under an open license acceptable to the Free Software Foundation (<http://gnu.org/licenses>) and/or the Open Source Initiative (<http://opensource.org/licenses>).
